slices.focus: Ariana wins a small preservation grant and moves from emergency mode to funded action
slices.summary: Ariana secures a local preservation grant covering archival boxes, dehumidifying supplies, and a part-time metadata assistant. Her role shifts from emergency reviewer to grant-backed project lead with a cataloging push and supply purchases.
open_loops: Drafting metadata template and assistant task list before the grant push starts
Defining success metrics for the short-term cataloging push
Building permissions tracking into the metadata workflow alongside physical stabilization
decisions: Ariana was now leading a grant-backed oral-history stabilization and cataloging push at Tremé Heritage Center, coordinat
Her personal finances were still tight, but the work grant reduced pressure by covering supplies and limited hourly help

slices.focus: Ariana sees a dermatologist for worsening eczema tied to archive work conditions
slices.summary: Ariana's knuckles crack from dust and repetitive handling during the grant-funded push. A dermatologist prescribes a structured steroid-ointment routine and cotton gloves. She plans to ask work for practical adjustments to reduce dust exposure and repetitive strain.
open_loops: Asking work for practical adjustments (shorter dusty blocks, station supplies)
Building a consistent ointment-and-gloves night routine
Preparing a three-line work conversation about the dermatologist findings
decisions: Her eczema now has a more structured treatment plan for hand flares after the dermatologist visit, replacing her earlier
